title: Permissible center predicate
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $B,M\subset X$ closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] defined by quasi-coherent ideals. The center $M$ is permissible in the boundary-contained sense if $M$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme], its support lies in that of $B$, and at every $x\in M$ there are an etale neighbourhood $v:W\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], $w\mapsto x$, an affine neighbourhood $U$ of $w$, and a regular system of parameters $(t_1,\ldots,t_d)$ in the Noetherian local ring $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. There are sections $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on $U$ whose germs are distinct members of this full system, with $v^{-1}B$ having ideal $(\prod_i f_i)$, and sections $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ whose germs are distinct members of the same full system, with $m\ge1$ and $v^{-1}M$ having ideal $(g_j:j=1,\ldots,m)$. The center parameters $g_j$ may include parameters that do not occur among the boundary factors $f_i$. This is the boundary-contained specialization of ILO VIII 4.1.2 used by the item; the predicate itself records exactly the regularity, containment and coordinate clauses.
